scenes.line1: Why do firewalls need two rules?
scenes.say: Why do firewalls sometimes need two rules for the same connection? What happens if you forget one?
Stateful firewalls track connections, so return traffic is allowed automatically. Stateless firewalls need rules for both directions.
When you file a firewall request, you need to specify the source, destination, port and protocol, direction, and a business reason.

scenes.title: Test your rule
scenes.say: After the rule is set, always verify access. Use netcat on Linux or Test-NetConnection on Windows.

scenes.question: Backend calls client—need a rule?
scenes.right: Yes, you need a rule for backend-to-client too.
scenes.say: Interview trap: If your backend calls back to the client, you need a rule in that direction too, or the connection will fail.
